newsitem.title: GERMANY: German intervention stores offered rye, barley.
newsitem.headline: German intervention stores offered rye, barley.

text.p: Some 53,098 tonnes of feed rye and 17,799 tonnes of barley have been offered to German intervention board BLE over the past fortnight, BLE sources said on Monday.
Traders said feed grain buyers' requirements had fallen. Where buying interest was evident, feed wheat was preferred.
Bread wheat and bread rye had attracted more free market buyers, so offers into intervention were small, they added.
Total offers in the November-May 1996/97 intervention season still lag those in the same 1995/96 period. By April 4 they had reached 921,094 tonnes, compared with 1,645,363 a year earlier.
The April buying-in price for all grains in 245.83 marks.
Total grain volumes physically delivered were roughly 697,000 tonnes at the end of March, compared with 1,507,000 a year earlier, BLE said.
Total stocks at that date -- including carry-in from 1995/96 -- were 1.28 million tonnes compared with 3.62 million a year earlier.
